source_ref: Gerber Y, Gentaz E, Malsert J (2022) PLOS ONE 17(10):e0276665, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0276665 (CC BY 4.0) -- Material section (14 items, 0 'never' to 4 'very often', French translation by the authors) and S1 Data (journal.pone.0276665.s001, RawData sheet, PREALT1-14/POSTALT1-14); item wording from Duerden MD, Witt PA, Fernandez M, Bryant MJ, Theriault D (2012) Journal of Youth Development 7(1):99-117, Table 1, https://jyd.pitt.edu/ojs/jyd/article/view/155 (CC BY 4.0); 14-item order corroborated by Rushton, Chrisjohn & Fekken (1981) Personality and Individual Differences 2:293-302 Table 1 and by the Urdu validation of Witt & Boleman (2009) in Pakistan Journal of Humanities and Social Sciences 10(3):1109-1120, Table 2; processing script data/gerber_2022_swiss_camp.py
note: SOURCE CHAIN. The study (Gerber, Gentaz & Malsert 2022, PLOS ONE 17(10):e0276665, CC BY 4.0) administered its OWN French translation ('It was freely translated into French by us for this study') and publishes exactly one item as an example ('I would give directions to someone I did not know'). I opened the deposit: S1 Data (journal.pone.0276665.s001) is a single 'RawData' sheet, 257x113, whose only text is the column headers (PREALT1..PREALT14 / POSTALT1..POSTALT14) -- no variable labels, no value labels, no French anywhere; s002-s005 are identical 50KB JavaScript blobs, not supplements. So the administered French is not recoverable in scope and the translated_substitute fallback applies: English in the base fields, _translated empty, language=French. TEXT. Item wording is transcribed verbatim from Table 1 ('Comparison of Original and Adapted Altruism Scale') of the adaptation's own source, Duerden, Witt, Fernandez, Bryant & Theriault (2012), Journal of Youth Development 7(1):99-117 -- reference [33] of the PLOS paper -- which jyd.pitt.edu licenses CC BY 4.0. ONE ITEM IS NOT VERBATIM AND IS IRW-RECONSTRUCTED: that table prints only 13 adapted items, marking Rushton's item 3 ('I have made change for a stranger') as dropped, while the SAME paper's reliability table counts the altruism measure at 14 items, and the Urdu translation/validation of the same Witt & Boleman (2009) 14-item scale (Pakistan Journal of Humanities and Social Sciences 10(3), 2022, Table 2) lists 14 items in that same order WITH 'make change for a stranger' at position 2. The JYD table therefore omits one adapted string. alt2's wording ('I would make change for someone I did not know.') was written by IRW following the adaptation's own transformation pattern ('a stranger' -> 'someone I did not know', past tense -> 'I would'); it is not a quotation. MAPPING. mapping_basis=reconstructed. data/gerber_2022_swiss_camp.py renames PREALT{i}/POSTALT{i} -> alt{i} number-preservingly, so alt{i} IS source column i; the inference is that source column i is instrument item i. The 14 retained items are exactly Rushton's 1981 items 2,3,4,6,9,10,11,13,14,16,17,18,19,20 in order (his 20 minus the six the adaptation drops), which is what makes the order recoverable at all. Checked against the data: PARTIAL, see verify_gerber_2022_altruism.R. OPTIONS. The paper states only the two anchors ('numbered from 0 (never) to 4 (very often)'), transcribed here in the paper's own lower case; resp 1, 2 and 3 ship with blank option_text rather than being padded with their own numbers. instructions is blank: no instruction text is published for the adapted form in either the PLOS paper or the JYD article, and Rushton's original instruction ('the frequency with which you have carried out the following acts') describes past behaviour, not the adaptation's intention framing, so it would have been wrong to borrow. RIGHTS. No restriction to quote. The wording was copied from a CC BY 4.0 article (jyd.pitt.edu: 'a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License ... allows others to copy, distribute, and transmit the Work'); the underlying SRA is reproduced in full on the first author's own site and carries no fee, no non-commercial clause and no redistribution bar, so neither 2026-09-04 ruling fires. TRANSLATION_SOURCE: official_instrument_english -- the English in the base fields is the instrument adaptation's own published English (Duerden et al. 2012 Table 1, the numbered items of the same Witt & Boleman form), not a rendering produced by this project. The single exception is alt2, whose adapted string that table omits and which IRW reconstructed; that item alone is IRW-generated content and is disclosed in public_note.
public_note: The item text shown here is the English wording of the Witt & Boleman adaptation of Rushton's Self-Report Altruism Scale; the study administered its own French translation, which it does not publish. One item is not a quotation: the source that documents the adaptation prints only 13 of its 14 adapted items, so alt2's wording was reconstructed by IRW from the dropped-item column of that table. Which statement each of alt1-alt14 refers to follows the instrument's published item order; the data pin alt8 (lowest corrected item-total correlation, 0.368 against 0.492 for the next lowest, matching the same item's lowest published loading in an independent validation) and the three floor and two ceiling items, but not the mid-range items alt3, alt4, alt10 and alt11, whose means sit within 0.27 of one another.
